description: A diff-context profile on an inline (review-mode) manifest renders prompts/diff.md with the profile's framing and scope, the manifest's range, excluded summary and diff, the rules partial listing every given principle and the registry ids, and the output_contract partial carrying the finding schema (without the rule-id enum, which the rules partial already lists) as compact JSON.

expected.prompt:
安全锐评: audit the diff for security vulnerabilities — focus on exploitable defects, not style.

Range: main...HEAD. 1 files excluded: 1 lockfile

Review the following git diff. Be BLUNT. Praise nothing that does not deserve it.

Rules (not exhaustive; also the repo's CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .claude/rules/). Every finding names in `rule` the ONE id below it violates; a defect no id names takes the closest principle.
Principles:
- first-principles: Derive from the actual system and current needs, not habit or precedent; state shaping assumptions.
- no-historical-baggage: Remove obsolete structures and dead paths no current need uses.
- occams-razor: Simplest design that fully meets the need; nothing for hypothetical needs.
- single-source-of-truth: Each fact lives in one place; everything else is derived from it.
- layered-decoupling: Depend one way through narrow interfaces; never into internals or upward.
- names-match-behaviour: A name says what the thing does now.
- no-backward-compatibility: No shims, aliases or dual paths for old callers; callers move with the change.
- progressive-disclosure: An entry point states what is needed first and points to detail; no duplication across levels.
- keep-valuable-options: Generality is a requirement: keep every parameter and option a real case uses or plausibly needs; Occam and no-baggage remove dead paths, never capability.
Registry rules (the family registry, by id): NAMED-SETS-NOT-COUNTS
Severity: HIGH is a defect that must not merge; MEDIUM and LOW never block. `security` is true for a security defect, whatever its severity.

Scope: Authorization / access-control gaps and missing authentication; Injection (SQL, command, template, XSS) and unsafe input handling; Hardcoded secrets / credentials / tokens; SSRF and path traversal; Unsafe deserialization; Crypto misuse (weak algorithms, static IVs, predictable randomness)

Respond with ONLY a JSON object { "findings": [...] }; an empty array means you found nothing. Each finding is one object conforming to this JSON Schema:
{"$schema":"https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema","title":"sharp-review reviewer finding","type":"object","required":["severity","security","rule","file","anchor","summary","category"],"properties":{"severity":{"type":"string","enum":["HIGH","MEDIUM","LOW"],"description":"HIGH blocks the merge until fixed or disposed; MEDIUM and LOW do not."},"security":{"type":"boolean","description":"true when the finding is a security defect; a security finding blocks the merge whatever its severity."},"rule":{"type":"string","description":"The ONE id this finding violates: a principle id or a registry rule id from the list above; an unknown id refuses the finding."},"file":{"type":"string","description":"The repo-relative path, no line number."},"anchor":{"type":"string","minLength":1,"description":"One line of the file the finding is about, copied VERBATIM (never a line number): with rule and file it is the finding's identity across review rounds."},"summary":{"type":"string"},"category":{"type":"string","enum":["Bug","Feature","Performance"]},"suggestion":{"type":"string"},"detail":{"type":"string"}}}
